title: Vendor risk & SOC2 prep notes (1:1)
content:
Purpose: prep for 1:1 with Jordan (audit lead) and follow-up notes. Goal: make sure vendor evidence and control mappings are ready for Q2 SOC2 readiness check and to surface any gaps for the SOC2 dry run.

Context / quick summary:
- Redwood is planning a Q2 dry run for SOC2. This 1:1 is to align on vendor evidence, responsibilities, and a prioritized remediation plan.
- Focus areas: vendor inventory completeness, contractual SLAs (data handling / breach notification), encryption/KMS evidence for private deployments, and change-history for config controls.

Top outcomes I want from this sync:
- Confirm which vendors are in-scope for the dry run vs deferred (high risk vs low risk).
- Agree on exact evidence artifacts we need to hand to the auditor for each vendor (contracts, DPA, pen test summary, SOC2/ISO reports).
- Identify 2–3 quick wins (<=2 weeks) to close low-effort gaps.
- Decide owners + tickets for the medium/long remediation items.

Talking points / checklist to run through in 1:1:
1) Vendor inventory sanity check
   - Latest CSV on Confluence (linked_artifacts) — ensure updated within last 30d.
   - Flags: any vendors without a DPA? (we think ~3: third-party monitoring, analytics, legacy auth).
   - Ask Jordan: do auditors require written risk acceptance for non-contractual vendors or is documented compensating control enough?

2) Evidence pack per vendor (minimum set)
   - Contract + DPA (signed)
   - Recent security report (SOC2, ISO27001, pentest) or alternative evidence (security questionnaire + SSAE attestation).
   - Data flows showing what customer data is shared (screenshot from integration diagram).
   - Encryption/KMS proof if the vendor can access customer data.
   - Last security incident/CVEs timeline (if any) + vendor remediation notes.
   - Evidence location: gdrive:shared_drives/company/misc/vendor-evidence/ or PR in infra repo for infra-facing vendors.

3) In-scope selection rules (proposal)
   - All vendors that process customer data or support production inference (models, logging, telemetry, metrics, alerting) = in-scope.
   - Vendors with admin access to infra (CI/CD, infra provisioning) = in-scope.
   - Low-risk tools (marketing analytics, recruitment ATS) = defer unless they store customer PII.

4) Quick wins (examples to propose)
   - Update DPA template and send to 3 outstanding vendors (owner: Legal / SLM outreach).
   - Add vendor evidence folder links to the vendor inventory row (owner: Alex M, due 2025-02-21).
   - Collect exported IAM logs for infra vendors for last 90 days (owner: SRE -> Ticket INFRA-782).

5) Harder gaps to schedule
   - Replace legacy monitoring vendor (no pen-test summary) or document compensating controls with signed risk acceptance (owner: Solutions Eng + Legal).
   - Formalize encrypted key management evidence for Private deployments (KMS key rotation logs) — owner: Platform Eng.

6) Auditor ask & timeline
   - Dry run scheduled for early Q2 (TBD). Need evidence snapshot 2 weeks before.
   - We'll create an "audit evidence collection" label in Drive and lock the set of files at snapshot time to avoid drifting.

Open questions / prompts for Jordan during 1:1:
- Which specific SOC2 controls (CC6/CC7? or the old mapping) do auditors emphasize for vendor risk this year? Any leanments toward ISO mapping?
- How formal does evidence need to be for internal tools? e.g., internal CI tool that has access to production — is runbook + IAM logs sufficient or do we need vendor attestation?
- For vendors without SOC/ISO reports, is the security questionnaire + 3rd-party penetration test summary generally acceptable?

Notes from quick evidence pre-check (my cursory review 2025-02-09):
- Vendor inventory CSV has 68 entries. 12 marked "needs evidence".
- 3 vendors definitely missing signed DPAs (analytics-2, legacy-auth, monitoring-old).
- Private deployment customers: make sure their KMS evidence and customer-specific configs are separated (we already have example folder template under private-deployments/).
- Infra vendors: most have basic SOC reports, but few have proof of key rotation or change-history exports.

Action items to create during or immediately after 1:1 (put into Jira with tags security-audit & vendor):
- SEC-XXXX: Update vendor inventory rows with evidence links (owner: Alex M, due 2025-02-21).
- SEC-XXXX: Reach out to 3 vendors for signed DPAs (owner: Legal - Priya, due 2025-03-07).
- INFRA-782: Export IAM and key-rotation logs for infra vendors (owner: SRE - Mateo, due 2025-02-28).
- PLAT-109: Add KMS key rotation proof and snapshot script for Private deploys (owner: Platform Eng - Priyanka, due 2025-03-14).
- DOC-45: Create audit evidence collection folder + README & label (owner: Zoe, due 2025-02-17).

Draft language for auditor requests (short) to include in evidence README:
"Please find bundled evidence for the 2025 Q2 SOC2 dry run. Files are organized by vendor and control. If a vendor does not provide a SOC/ISO report, we have included a completed security questionnaire and available pen-test summaries. Contact security@redwood.com for any clarifications."

Meeting follow-ups (what I will do in next 48h):
- Create initial evidence collection folder and README (DOC-45).
- Triage vendor-inventory "needs evidence" rows and assign them.
- Draft the outreach email template for DPAs and non-SOC vendors (share with Legal + Jordan).

Notes-to-self / reminders:
- Don't assume infra PRs include audit-friendly history—capture squash PRs separately if needed.
- When requesting logs, specify time range (90d) and format (CSV or JSON) and include checksum.
- Keep auditor timestamps consistent (UTC).

Relevant links to paste/send in meeting:
- Vendor inventory (confluence): https://confluence.redwood/integration/vendor-inventory
- Sample evidence folder structure: gdrive/shared_drives/company/misc/vendor-evidence/template
- Infra PR example for log export: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/452

End notes: this is a rough personal scratchpad. Will clean up and push owners into Jira after 1:1. Need Jordan to confirm dry run date window so we can lock snapshot date.
